title: 5 Things to Know Before Hiring an Interior Designer in Rajkot
excerpt: Planning to hire an interior designer in Rajkot? Here is what every homeowner should know before signing a contract.
content:
Hiring an interior designer is one of the most significant decisions you make when building or renovating a home. In Rajkot, where the design market has grown rapidly over the last decade, knowing what to look for can save you time, money, and a great deal of frustration.

At VOAD Architecture & Interiors, we have worked with homeowners across Rajkot and Gujarat who came to us after difficult experiences with other studios. These five things are what they wish someone had told them first.

1. Portfolio speaks louder than promises

Any designer can present a beautiful mood board assembled from Pinterest. What matters is evidence of completed work: real projects, real spaces, real finishes. Ask to see a portfolio of completed projects similar in scale and style to what you have in mind. If a designer specialises in commercial interiors but you want a warm family home, that matters.

Pay attention to consistency. A designer whose work looks dramatically different across every project may lack a coherent design language, which can translate to an incoherent result for you. Look for a clear visual point of view across different project types and scales.

2. Understand exactly what the fee covers

Interior design fees in Rajkot are typically structured in one of three ways: a flat project fee, a percentage of the total project cost, or an hourly rate. Each has implications. A flat fee gives you certainty upfront. A percentage fee means the designer benefits financially from higher spending, which can create a subtle conflict of interest. An hourly rate can reward slow work.

More importantly, clarify what the fee does not include. Does it cover site visits? Procurement? Contractor coordination? Revisions beyond a certain number? Get this in writing before work begins. Ambiguity about fee scope is one of the most common sources of conflict between clients and designers in Gujarat.

3. Ask who will actually be working on your project

Many larger design firms sell on the strength of a senior designer's reputation and then hand the project to junior staff. You meet the principal at the pitch and rarely see them again. This is one reason we keep VOAD deliberately small: Ar. Vivek Bosmiya is the designer on every project, not a manager reviewing junior work. Whoever you hire, make sure you know who will be on site and who will be making day-to-day decisions.

4. Check references, not just website testimonials

Testimonials are curated. Ask for direct contact details of two or three previous clients and call them. Ask specific questions: Did the project finish on time? Was the final cost close to the estimate? Were there things the designer could have handled better? A confident designer will have no hesitation giving you references. If a studio is reluctant to connect you with past clients, treat that as meaningful information.

5. Clarify the timeline from the start

Interior projects in Rajkot routinely run over schedule, often because timelines were optimistic to begin with or because no single person was accountable for keeping contractors on track. Ask for a written project schedule with milestones, and ask how delays are communicated and managed.

A project that takes three months longer than planned is not a good result, regardless of how it looks at the end. Realistic timelines, shared in writing from the start, protect both sides.

6. Know what a realistic Rajkot interior project costs

Interior design costs in Rajkot vary widely depending on scope and specification. A basic bedroom or living room fit-out by a competent local contractor may run between Rs. 800 and Rs. 1,500 per square foot for materials and labour. A mid-range residential project managed by a professional design studio typically falls between Rs. 1,500 and Rs. 2,500 per square foot. High-specification work with custom joinery, imported materials, or extensive false ceiling treatments can go considerably higher.

These figures cover materials and execution and do not include the designer's professional fee, which is usually charged separately. Being honest about your budget from the first meeting allows a designer to tell you clearly whether your expectations are achievable for what you want to build. A good designer will not take on a project whose budget cannot support the quality you have in mind. A clear budget conversation at the start saves time for everyone involved.

7. Look for local material knowledge

Gujarat has a strong tradition of craft and material production. Rajkot and the surrounding region offer access to local stone, handmade tiles, skilled woodworkers, and a network of craftsmen with deep trade experience. A designer with genuine local knowledge can source these materials thoughtfully and use them in ways that suit both the design vision and the Gujarat climate.

Ask any designer you are considering how familiar they are with local sourcing across Rajkot and Ahmedabad. A studio that relies entirely on branded showrooms and national catalogues may be missing the most interesting and cost-effective options available locally. The best residential interiors in Gujarat almost always combine national-quality design thinking with materials and craft that are rooted in the region.

If you are planning an interior project in Rajkot or Gujarat and would like to discuss your space, get in touch with us. We are happy to answer questions before you commit to anything.
author: Ar. Vivek Bosmiya

title: How to Restore a Heritage Haveli in Gujarat
excerpt: Heritage havelis across Gujarat are slowly disappearing, not for lack of resources but for lack of the right approach. Here is what restoration actually involves.
content:
Gujarat has a remarkable built heritage. From the ornate havelis of Kutch to the step-well architecture of Patan, the state contains some of the finest examples of traditional Indian craftsmanship. Yet far too many of these buildings are quietly falling apart, not for lack of resources but for lack of the right approach.

Restoring a heritage haveli is fundamentally different from renovating a modern home. The decisions you make in the first few weeks set the course for everything that follows. Treating a heritage structure like a standard renovation project is the most common mistake owners make, and it is one that is very difficult to undo.

Start with a structural assessment

Before any restoration work begins, a qualified structural engineer must assess the building. Heritage structures often use load-bearing walls, lime mortar, and timber frames that behave very differently from modern reinforced concrete. Cracks that look alarming may be superficial. Sections that look intact may be significantly compromised. You need a professional assessment, not a visual guess from a contractor who primarily builds new construction.

Document everything before you touch it

Photograph and measure every element of the original structure before any intervention. Original jaali work, carved brackets, hand-painted plasterwork, stone thresholds: these details are irreplaceable once lost. Documentation also gives you a reference point if restoration work needs to be halted and resumed later, which is common on larger properties. A complete photographic and measured record costs very little relative to what it protects.

Work with conservation-aware architects

Not every architect has experience with heritage structures. Look for professionals who understand traditional construction techniques, are familiar with Gujarat-specific materials like Dhrangadhra stone and lime-pozzolana plasters, and have worked on projects reviewed by heritage bodies. At VOAD, heritage design is one of our core specialisations, and we approach every heritage project with the same documentation-first discipline. The wrong architect can cause more damage in two months than decades of neglect.

Respect the original materials

The single most common mistake in heritage restoration is replacing traditional materials with modern substitutes. Lime plaster gets replaced with cement. Teak joinery gets replaced with aluminium. Hand-carved stone gets replaced with cast concrete replicas. These substitutions look wrong, perform badly in the same climate the original materials were designed for, and can cause long-term structural damage by trapping moisture in ways lime construction was never meant to handle. Source period-appropriate materials even when they are harder to find and more expensive to use.

Navigate heritage regulations early

If the structure is listed or sits in a heritage zone, you will need approvals before any modification. The process in Gujarat can take time, particularly for structures under ASI or state heritage board jurisdiction. Start this paperwork as early as possible, ideally before you have committed to a contractor or a timeline. Your architect should know which permissions apply to your specific property and how long the approval process typically takes in that jurisdiction.

Understand what restoration costs in Gujarat

Heritage restoration is typically more expensive per square foot than new construction, and the range is wide. A basic structural stabilisation and waterproofing project on a small haveli in Gujarat may start at Rs. 1,200 per square foot. A full restoration that involves carved stone repair, lime plaster reinstatement, and custom woodwork to match the original can reach Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 5,000 per square foot or more, depending on the extent of craft detail and the availability of craftsmen skilled in the specific techniques required.

The cost is driven heavily by the condition of the structure, the extent of missing or damaged original material, and the scarcity of the skills involved. Get a detailed scope and cost estimate from your architect before committing to a timeline. Surprises are common in restoration work; a well-prepared estimate will include a contingency for the unexpected, typically 15 to 20 percent of the project cost.

Plan for ongoing maintenance

Heritage buildings require long-term care. The restoration process is not a one-time event after which the building takes care of itself. Lime plasterwork needs periodic attention. Timber frames require protection from humidity and seasonal pests. Roofs need inspection and repointing after each monsoon season in Gujarat, where rainfall can be intense and concentrated.

The most successful heritage restorations we have seen across Gujarat are those where the owners commit to a maintenance plan from the start, rather than treating restoration as a renovation that, once complete, requires nothing further. A well-maintained restored haveli can serve as a family home, a heritage stay, a cultural space, or a combination of uses for generations. The investment in careful restoration pays back in durability and character in a way no new construction can replicate.

If you are considering the restoration of a heritage property in Gujarat and want to understand what the process looks like for your specific building, contact VOAD. We are glad to discuss scope and complexity before you take on any commitment.

title: Bungalow vs Villa: What Suits the Gujarat Climate?
excerpt: Gujarat's heat, monsoon, and mild winters demand architectural respect. Choosing the right home form affects how comfortable and costly your home is to live in.
content:
One of the most common questions we hear from clients planning a new home in Rajkot is whether to build a bungalow or a villa. The answer is rarely about budget alone. It depends on the site, the family, and most importantly, the climate.

Gujarat has a climate that demands architectural respect. Summers regularly exceed 42 degrees Celsius in Rajkot. Monsoon brings intense but concentrated rainfall between June and September. Winters are mild but occasionally cool at night. The right design choice significantly affects how comfortable and how costly your home is to live in year-round, and the difference compounds over decades.

What defines each type

In Gujarat's residential market, a bungalow typically refers to a ground-floor or single-storey home with a private plot, garden, and car parking. A villa more often describes a two or three-storey home on a standalone plot or within a gated compound, usually with a contemporary facade and more vertical floor planning. These terms are used loosely by developers and agents in Rajkot, so clarify with your architect exactly what you mean when you use either word.

How bungalows perform in Gujarat's climate

A well-designed bungalow handles the Gujarat climate more naturally. The single storey allows for a wide roof overhang, which shades the walls and windows during peak summer. Cross-ventilation is easier to achieve when the entire living area is on one level. Courtyard-style bungalows, common in traditional Gujarati home design, create natural cooling through convection and shade interior spaces that would otherwise bake in direct sun. On large plots in established Rajkot neighbourhoods, the bungalow form is often the more thermally comfortable choice, particularly for families who spend significant time at home during the day.

How villas perform in Gujarat's climate

Multi-storey villas concentrate more living area on a smaller footprint, which is an advantage on smaller urban plots in central Rajkot where land is expensive. However, upper floors accumulate more heat in summer unless the design specifically addresses solar gain through insulated roofs, recessed windows, double-glazed western facades, or strategic vegetation on the building perimeter. A villa designed without careful attention to Gujarat's climate will require more mechanical cooling, which means higher electricity costs throughout a long summer. The upper-floor bedroom that seemed like a luxury in the showroom becomes a liability at 2 am in April.

What matters most: orientation and materials

Regardless of form, orientation and material selection matter more than building type. A home with its main living areas facing west in Rajkot will struggle in summer regardless of whether it is a bungalow or villa. Light-coloured exterior finishes, thick wall construction, double glazing on western facades, and adequate roof insulation make a measurable difference to interior temperatures across the year. See our project portfolio for examples of how we address these factors across both building types and a range of plot orientations in Rajkot.

Typical plot sizes and costs in Rajkot

In Rajkot's established residential neighbourhoods, bungalow plots commonly range from 200 to 500 square yards. A well-designed bungalow on a 300 square yard plot can comfortably accommodate four bedrooms, generous living and dining areas, a garden, and covered parking. Construction costs for a good-quality bungalow in Rajkot typically start at around Rs. 1,800 to Rs. 2,500 per square foot for structure and standard finishes, with premium interiors and landscape adding to this figure.

Villa developments in Rajkot are more common in planned townships and gated communities on the city's outskirts, where plots are standardised and community infrastructure such as security and landscaping is shared. The compact footprint of a villa makes better use of a smaller plot in a premium location, though upper-floor living requires careful attention to the thermal management considerations described above. Get an independent cost estimate before committing to a developer's quoted rate.

The architect's role in climate performance

The difference between a home that stays comfortable without constant air conditioning and one that demands it from April to October almost always comes down to decisions made at the design stage. Wall thickness, window placement and size, roof insulation specification, shading devices, and the position of service spaces relative to living areas are all far cheaper to get right from the start than to retrofit later. If you are building a new home in Rajkot, invest time early in understanding how the building will perform thermally across Gujarat's seasons, not only how it will look in a render.

Making the right choice for your family

A family that wants ground-floor living for elderly members and young children will find a bungalow more practical. A family prioritising a compact footprint, a private upper-level primary suite, or a specific gated community will find a villa layout more appropriate. The best answer depends on your specific plot, family size, and how you intend to use the space day to day across all seasons.

If you are at the planning stage and want to discuss which form suits your plot and lifestyle, get in touch with VOAD. We work across both building types and have completed projects in Rajkot and across Gujarat.
author: Ar. Vivek Bosmiya

title: What Does a Turnkey Interior Project Actually Include?
excerpt: The word turnkey gets used loosely in the design industry. Here is exactly what it means at VOAD and what you should expect from any studio that offers it.
content:
The word turnkey gets used loosely in the design and construction industry. Some firms use it to mean they will coordinate the contractors. Others mean they handle everything from the initial design sketch to the day you receive the keys. The difference matters enormously when you are planning a project and comparing studios in Rajkot or across Gujarat.

At VOAD Architecture & Interiors, turnkey means one thing: you hand over the brief and we handle everything until the space is ready to live or work in. Here is exactly what that covers.

Design and space planning

The process begins with a detailed brief and site measurement. We develop floor plans, elevation drawings, 3D visualisations, and material boards so you can see the complete vision before any work starts on site. Every change and approval happens at this stage, reducing the chance of expensive modifications during construction. Nothing begins on site until you have signed off on the design in full.

Material selection and procurement

We source and procure all materials: flooring, wall finishes, ceiling treatments, hardware, lighting fixtures, sanitaryware, and cabinetry. We work with suppliers across Rajkot, Ahmedabad, and nationally to find materials that suit both the design and the budget. You see the materials and samples before they are purchased. Nothing is ordered without your specific approval, and we maintain a full procurement log throughout the project.

Contractor coordination

We manage the civil and finishing contractors directly. This includes scheduling, site supervision, quality checks at each stage, and resolving the day-to-day problems that always arise on site. You do not need to visit the site daily or manage workers yourself. We are present on site so you do not have to be, and we provide regular updates so you always know where the project stands.

Furniture, furnishings, and styling

A turnkey project includes furniture selection and procurement: sofas, beds, dining tables, storage units, soft furnishings, and decor. We source pieces that are consistent with the design intent and the budget, not afterthoughts purchased from the nearest showroom. The final styling of the space, including the placement of objects and accessories, is part of the handover process. See completed examples of turnkey work across residential and commercial projects in our project portfolio.

The handover

When we hand over a turnkey project, the space is ready to use. We walk you through every system, fixture, and finish. We provide a snag list and return to address any items that need adjustment within an agreed period. The project is not considered complete until you are satisfied with every detail of the delivered space.

What a typical turnkey timeline looks like

A well-managed turnkey interior project in Rajkot for a three-bedroom home or apartment typically takes between 12 and 18 weeks from design sign-off to handover. A larger home or a more complex brief will take longer. The design phase, which includes drawings, 3D visualisations, material selection, and client approvals, usually accounts for 3 to 4 weeks. Civil work including flooring, false ceilings, electrical runs, and plumbing takes 5 to 8 weeks on a well-managed site. Furniture procurement, delivery, and final styling account for the remaining time.

Delays most commonly occur when client approvals are slow at key decision points, or when materials have long lead times from suppliers outside Rajkot. The fastest projects are always those where the client is available and decisive during the design phase. We provide a detailed project timeline at the start of every engagement so expectations on both sides are clear from the first week.

What turnkey does not include

It is equally important to be clear about what a turnkey interior contract does not cover. External landscaping and garden design, structural changes to the building such as adding rooms or removing load-bearing walls, and long-term maintenance services after handover are typically outside the scope of an interior turnkey contract. Appliances and home electronics are usually excluded unless specifically agreed and listed in the contract. If any of these are important to your project, discuss them before the contract is signed, not after work has started on site.

Is turnkey the right choice for your project?

Turnkey works best for clients who are time-constrained, based outside Rajkot during the project, or who simply prefer to delegate the full complexity of a build or fit-out to a professional team they trust. It is not always the right choice for clients who want to be directly involved in sourcing materials, visiting showrooms, or managing their own contractor relationships. A good studio will tell you honestly whether a turnkey contract suits your project and your working style, rather than recommending it as the default option for every client. Browse our completed turnkey projects to get a clear sense of the quality and scope you can expect from VOAD.

If you are considering a turnkey interior project in Rajkot or Gujarat and want to understand the timeline and investment involved, contact VOAD. We are happy to give you a realistic picture before you make any decision.
